what: Transitions: what happens at each section change. cues is the FX bed policy (arrange.generate_fx_cues): for each moment (into_drop, into_build, break_start, groove_start, outro_start, intro_end) a list of cue templates (kinds: impact, air_sweep, noise_riser, tone_riser, downlifter, sub_drop, reverse_cymbal, noise_wash). transitions are production-recipe moves added for section pairs (recipes: filter_sweep, reverb_throw, gap, lowpass_open, lowpass_dip, filter_wobble, pitch_rise, fade_in, stutter_fill, reverse_fill, tape_stop, fx_swell).

options.label: Noise and tone risers, impact and air sweep into each drop
options.what: The current default: an 8-bar noise riser and a tone riser through every build, an impact and a reverse-cymbal air sweep on the drop, downlifters out. Effective and familiar; use it when the song is a club record.

sources.where: risers, impacts and snare rolls before each drop

options.label: A beat of silence, then a sub drop and an impact
options.what: No riser at all: the build thins out, the last beat before the drop is silent (everything gapped), the drop lands with a sub-drop sweep and a short impact. Restraint makes the drop louder.

sources.where: SFX Mega Sub, SFX Noise Punch on the drop

options.label: Low-passed music opening into the drop, master reverb in the breakdown
options.what: Trance's way in: the breakdown runs with the master reverb up and the bass and kick low-passed; through the build the low-pass opens over 8 to 16 bars, the snare roll climbs, and the drop is the filter fully open.

sources.where: Filter - Kick cutoff clips, Filter - Bass Bus cutoff, Reeverb 2 - Master wet level, Filter - Master cutoff

options.label: Reverse cymbals and filter swells, no risers
options.what: For songs without drops: a reverse cymbal into each new phrase, a low-pass dipping and reopening on the music, reverb throws on the last word of a vocal phrase. Nothing synthetic shouts.

sources.where: reverb and delay throws through short automation clips, filter sweeps

options.label: Pitched snare roll and a tape stop
options.what: The build is a snare roll whose pitch rises an octave; the bar before the drop stops like a tape (Gross Beat slot 18) or stutters; the drop lands dry with no impact.

sources.where: 808 Snare roll with pitch automation, GROSS BEAT clips

options.label: Block marks: a drum-fill sample, a riser, an impact on the block edge
options.what: In loop-block songs the edges are marked, not built: a one-bar drum fill and a short riser into the block, an impact on its first beat, nothing else.

sources.where: FX - Gunshot, Riser, Riser 2, Drum Fill clips at block edges

options.label: Reverse piano chord, wind rise, sub impact
options.what: Musical FX from the song's own sounds: a reversed chord swelling into the downbeat, a wind riser, a sub impact under the first kick. Drum and bass and cinematic records use them instead of white noise.

sources.where: Piano Reverse, Wind Fx, Sub Impact, Tombak Reverse

options.manual: A reversed chord of the song's own pads is the best version: bounce two bars of the pad, reverse it in Edison, place it to end on the drop.

options.label: Radio filter on the vocal before the chorus
options.what: The vocal (or an ad-lib) band-passed like a radio for the last bar before the chorus, panned by automation, then full again on the chorus: the reggaeton and pop lift without a build.

sources.where: 2 Radio ad-libs: filtered chops with panning automation, own delay send

options.label: A stop bar: everything out but a noise sweep and the last word
options.what: No 8-bar risers and no impacts: the bar before each drop empties (drums, bass and music gapped), a one-bar white-noise sweep rises through it, the vocal's last words hang in the space, and the drop comes back on the downbeat. Contrast by subtraction.

sources.where: bars 28 and 52: drums and music out, noise sweep (spectral flatness 0.08 to 0.09, centroid 3.8 to 4.8 kHz), the chorus's last words
